sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 1.5% a year from $41.9 billion in FY2016 to $47.9 billion in FY2025 [F1][F10][F219], a flat decade interrupted by refranchising and the pandemic.
The FY2017-FY2018 step down of 13.5% and 5.3% [D42][D93] reflects bottling refranchising; the table's FY2017 and FY2018 revenue are later recasts, not the figures first reported [R1][F2][X2][F3][X3].
Revenue fell 11.4% in FY2020 [D195] as the pandemic hit away-from-home channels, then rebounded 17.1% in FY2021 [D246] on concentrate volume growth of 9% [P49].
FY2025 revenue rose 1.9% [D449] while operating income jumped 37.7% [D450], driven by lower other operating charges after the prior-year fairlife contingent consideration remeasurement [P12].
Concentrate operations supplied 59.4% of FY2025 revenue [D532] and 1.6pp of growth [D534], while finished product operations added only 0.3pp [D541].
Non-US concentrate operations grew 3.1% and contributed 1.3pp [D547][D548], against a 4.9% decline in non-US finished product operations that subtracted 1.0pp [D554][D555].
North America is the largest segment at 40.9% of revenue [D611], but its FY2025 growth slowed to 3.8% and 1.5pp of contribution [D612][D613].
Worldwide concentrate sales volume grew 1% in FY2025 with unit case volume even [P16], and pricing initiatives plus that volume drove the operating income increase [P12].

Profit outran revenue: operating income grew 5.3% a year against 1.5% for revenue over the window [F221][F219], and diluted EPS CAGR of 8.2% [F224] matched net income's 8.1% [F222] as the diluted share count fell only 0.2% in FY2025 [D468].
Operating margin reached a window high of 28.7% in FY2025 [F50][D765], 2.7pp above the 26.0% median [D766] and far above the 20.7% low [D764].

Gross margin of 61.6% [F30] sits 0.9pp above its 60.7% median [D772], with the FY2025 gain of 0.6pp [D462] coming from pricing and prior-year refranchising, partly offset by currency and commodities [P14].

The FY2025 operating margin rose 7.5pp [D463], of which 6.2pp came from other lines [D477] as other operating charges fell after the FY2024 fairlife remeasurement [P12]; SG&A added 0.7pp [D476] on lower foundation contributions and incentive expense [P13].
The largest adverse move was FY2024's 3.5pp margin decline [D413], when higher commodity costs, SG&A and other operating charges plus an 11% currency headwind cut operating income 12% [P25].
Net margin of 27.3% [F70] tracked operating margin closely, with a 17.9% effective tax rate [D435] and $1.1 billion of other income [X100] offsetting $1.7 billion of interest expense [X70].
Free cash flow was only 0.40x net income in FY2025 [D437], the window low [D776] and far below the 0.97x median [D778].
Operating cash flow rose 8.9% to $7.4 billion [D454][F100] on strong cash operating results, lower tax payments and working-capital timing, partly offset by prior-year factoring benefits [P1].
The FY2024 collapse to $6.8 billion [F99] was driven by a $6.0 billion IRS tax litigation deposit [P22], and conversion has not recovered since.
Capex of $2.1 billion was 4.4% of revenue [F110][D432] and 2.01x D&A [D438], the highest ratio in the window, so capital intensity now exceeds depreciation.
Net cash of $8.8 billion, 18.3% of revenue [D442][D443], ranks at the 100th percentile against six staples peers whose median is -14.5% [D793][D794].
The swing from $32.4 billion of net debt in FY2023 [D341] to net cash reflects a total-debt figure of $1.5 billion in FY2025 [D441], up 31.3% from FY2024 [D470].
Buybacks plus dividends of $9.5 billion were 179.9% of free cash flow [D444][D445], funded from the balance sheet, and the diluted share count fell just 0.2% [D468].
Dividends of $8.8 billion [X145] dwarfed $746 million of buybacks [X135], and return on average equity of 46.0% [D448] exceeded the 36.5% peer median [D798].

The revenue basis break is the most serious: FY2017 and FY2018 in the table are recasts ($36.2 billion and $34.3 billion) versus $35.4 billion and $31.9 billion first reported [R1][F2][X2][F3][X3], so growth spanning those years mixes presentations.
Payout exceeded free cash flow for three straight years, at 105.1%, 214.2% and 179.9% [R2][D344][D395][D445], leaving capital return dependent on balance-sheet cash.
Free cash flow ran below 80% of net income in FY2024 and FY2025, at 0.45x and 0.40x [R3][D387][D437], the weakest conversion in the window.
Total debt rose 31.3% in FY2025 [R4][D470], though from a $1.1 billion base [D391] that keeps leverage immaterial.

Free cash flow to net income: a recovery toward the 0.97x window median [D778] from 0.40x [D437] would confirm the FY2025 operating-cash rebound; another year near 0.40x would entrench the conversion problem, visible in the FY2026 cash-flow statement.
Operating margin: holding at or above the 26.0% median [D766] after the 28.7% high [F50] would show the FY2025 charge relief is durable rather than one-off, in the FY2026 income statement.

Buybacks plus dividends against free cash flow: a move back toward the 94.4% FY2019 level [D140] from 179.9% [D445] would signal capital return is again self-funded, in the FY2026 cash-flow statement.
